Docs/Replay/Guide

Replay

Asset references, caches and exchange

3 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

Use assets.Ref to refer to immutable payload bytes from gameplay state without copying those bytes into every frame. It contains a SHA-256 ID and byte count, and is suitable for a frame, canonical schema or checkpoint. Payload bytes live in an independently owned Cache. A new payload gets a new ID; receiving an asset never changes simulation state.

cache_put owns a copy and validates an expected reference when supplied. cache_read / cache_copy return copies so ordinary reads cannot mutate content under an existing hash. Cache capacity and invalid data leave previous entries intact. Pins protect current dependencies; release pins and explicitly discard entries that are no longer needed. Destroy the cache when its lifetime ends.

Mesh exchanges missing watched references with explicitly bound peers. Its name does not require a full network mesh: bind only the authority on clients, and the admitted client connections on the authority. Simultaneous requests travel in both directions. Once the authority caches a player's asset, it can supply later joiners; a surviving cached copy can serve after a new authority/binding is installed.

Odin
assets.mesh_init(&mesh, &cache, application_wire)
assets.mesh_bind(&mesh, admitted_peer, scope)
assets.mesh_watch(&mesh, needed_references[:])
assets.mesh_frame(&mesh, monotonic_ms)

The watched working set is requested and public to bound peers. mesh_publish keeps earlier cached revisions available without pinning or requesting them. An optional per-peer authorizer further restricts serving and is rechecked during a transfer; revocation cancels remaining output. An optional content validator runs before installation. The frame reference is the expected content identity, not a file path supplied by a sender.

The default profile has 32 cached entries, 128 KiB per asset, a 4 MiB cache and 32 watched references. Up to 16 bound peers share 64 KiB/s output, 16 KiB per update, a 32 KiB burst, at most four requests per update and one new payload encoding per update. Ingress is limited to 64 packets/128 KiB per update. Each bound receiver allocates only the configured asset limit plus framing. Cache exhaustion is explicit; there is no implicit eviction of assets used by another subsystem.

mesh_watch pins cached dependencies without duplicating pins on repeated calls. Supply retained-history/checkpoint references as well as the current visible set when those lifetimes require them. mesh_complete reports byte availability for the working set. A missing asset remains missing rather than becoming guessed content. Applications can display a placeholder while requests retry.

The Godot Session_Assets facade sets up the optional application lane, binds the admitted roster and rebuilds peer workers on transport/authority changes while keeping the cache. Call session_assets_enable on options before opening Session or Room, and session_assets_frame after its frame pump, including fenced frames. It does not infer dependencies from arbitrary game types. Use a save bundle with the complete dependency set when persisting a world and its payloads.

png_info preflights PNG signature, IHDR CRC, dimensions and encoding fields before pixel allocation. It does not replace a full decoder. Godot's asset_png_image then validates/decodes the complete image. Defaults cap compressed bytes at 128 KiB, dimensions at 2048 and pixels at 1,048,576; bounds are configurable. The header and CRC rules follow the W3C PNG specification.

Native fault tests cover bidirectional transfer, late caches, source loss/new epoch, stale requests, private unadvertised cache entries, per-peer policy and content rejection. mesh_announce offers locally cached content before its ID enters gameplay. Offer acceptance is opt-in per admitted peer, with one pending offer per peer, bounded requests and a timeout. The Godot facade accepts offers from admitted players, not observers; its cache is specifically for public room assets. Earlier cached revisions remain available through the facade after a working-set change. Use a separate cache or a per-peer authorizer for private content.

The network model's authority-only action_admit hook can require the validated bytes before accepting a reference-setting action. Its decision enters the action ledger; prediction/replay do not consult mutable caches. Scrapyard uses that hook, then gates coordinator preparation on the checkpoint's image dependencies.

These are transport/cache guarantees; each game must supply complete save dependencies and prove its recovery/browser behavior with integration gates.
